To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) cycle-GAN can be successfully used for MR-CT DIR of the abdomen, but (ii) it fails to register the thoracic region due to the large lung volume changes which it synthesizes.

(1) cycle-GANs learn the intensity mapping between CT and MR images well, (2) the learned intensity map can be used for DIR, (3) cycle-GAN can synthesize the spatial information, which is not present in the training data, (4) the synthesized spatial information is not always accurate, (5) the synthesized spatial changes can be reduced by decreasing the spatial information provided in the discriminator.

(1) cycle-GANs can be used to synthesize MR images from CT images with a high degree of similarity and (2) the resulting images can be used for DIR, if the spatial information is restricted to the local neighborhood of the discriminator, and if the synthesized images are restricted to the abdominal region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of cycle-GAN on DIR.
a novel application of cycle-GANs, which is the generation of 3D MR images from unpaired CT data.
the impact of the cycle-GAN based image synthesis on DIR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cycle-GANs can be used to synthesize MR images from CT images, which can be registered to the CT with state-of-the-art DIR algorithms.
cycle-GANs are a promising tool for MR-CT DIR, but the current implementation is not ready for clinical application.
the use of cycle-GANs for DIR is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cycle-GAN is capable of synthesizing 3D MRIs of good quality, which are useful for DIR, provided that large deformations are not present.
cycle-GANs are able to learn the MR-CT intensity relationship and can be successfully applied in DIR for abdominal organs.
cycle-GANs can synthesize MRIs with a good anatomical appearance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cycle-GAN can synthesize MRIs from CTs and vice versa, but that it does not perform well for DIR, due to the lack of dense ground truth.
the cycle-GAN is a promising method for MR-CT synthesis for DIR.
, while GANs can learn the MR-CT intensity relationship, the synthesized images are not yet suitable for registration.
